dedupe_keys.name: global waste management outlook 2024 unep and iswa municipal solid waste generation costs and scenarios to 2050

description: The Global Waste Management Outlook 2024, published by the United Nations Environment Programme with the International Solid Waste Association on 28 February 2024, updates global estimates of waste generation and the cost of waste management since 2018. The report page read on 2026-09-28 states that municipal solid waste generation is predicted to grow from 2.1 billion tonnes in 2023 to 3.8 billion tonnes by 2050, that the direct global cost of waste management was about USD 252 billion in 2020 (USD 361 billion with the hidden costs of pollution, poor health and climate change) and could reach USD 640.3 billion a year by 2050, and that life cycle modelling compares three scenarios, business as usual, halfway measures and a circular economy, whose net annual cost ranges from USD 270.2 billion to a net gain of USD 108.5 billion. Coverage is global and regional. Access is a free PDF report with executive summaries in six languages; no licence is stated. Caveats: figures are modelled estimates, not facility data, regional detail is aggregated, and the underlying data tables are not offered separately. It supports capacity planning of waste collection and treatment and long-term scenario inputs for waste infrastructure studies. No related global waste outlook record is catalogued; city and country waste statistics complement it.
